questions.title: A newborn with masculinized (ambiguous) female external genitalia is found to have hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. Which enzyme deficiency is most consistent with this presentation?
questions.question: A newborn with masculinized (ambiguous) female external genitalia is found to have hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. Which enzyme deficiency is most consistent with this presentation?

explanations.A: Correct. Classic salt-wasting 21-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency (the most common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia) blocks cortisol and aldosterone synthesis, shunting precursors into the androgen pathway; the resulting excess fetal androgens virilize a genetically female fetus's external genitalia, while the aldosterone deficiency causes a salt-wasting crisis with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia in the newborn period. This combination of ambiguous genitalia in a genetic female plus salt-wasting electrolyte disturbance is the classic exam presentation for this enzyme defect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 5-alpha-reductase deficiency impairs conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and causes undervirilized external genitalia in genetic males, not virilization of a female fetus, and it does not cause a salt-wasting electrolyte disturbance.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aromatase deficiency impairs estrogen synthesis and can virilize a female fetus through unopposed androgen action, but it does not impair aldosterone synthesis and so does not produce this salt-wasting electrolyte picture.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes excess mineralocorticoid effect with hypertension and hypokalemia (the opposite electrolyte pattern) and undervirilization, not virilization, of a genetic female.

questions.learning_objective: 21-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes aldosterone deficiency and salt-wasting hyponatremia, alongside virilization of a genetic female fetus

questions.title: A 2-year-old boy has a testicular mass. Histology shows glomeruloid (Schiller-Duval) bodies. Which serum marker is most characteristically elevated?
questions.question: A 2-year-old boy has a testicular mass. Histology shows glomeruloid (Schiller-Duval) bodies. Which serum marker is most characteristically elevated?

explanations.A: Correct. Yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumor is the most common testicular germ cell tumor of infancy and early childhood, and it characteristically secretes alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), which serves as a reliable serum marker for diagnosis and treatment monitoring. Histologically it is distinguished by glomeruloid Schiller-Duval bodies, structures resembling primitive glomeruli that reflect the tumor's yolk-sac-like differentiation. This marker-histology pairing is a classic pediatric oncology teaching point.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Beta-hCG is the classic marker for choriocarcinoma, a different, more aggressive germ cell tumor type, not for yolk sac tumor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. PSA is a marker for prostatic tissue (benign or malignant) and has no relevance to a pediatric testicular germ cell tumor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. CA-125 is an ovarian tumor marker, most associated with epithelial ovarian carcinoma, not with testicular germ cell tumors.

questions.title: A woman presents with vulvar thickening; biopsy shows epidermal thinning with underlying dermal fibrosis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.question: A woman presents with vulvar thickening; biopsy shows epidermal thinning with underlying dermal fibrosis. What is the diagnosis?

explanations.A: Correct. Lichen sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis of the vulva, most common in postmenopausal women, that produces a thin, whitish, parchment-like epidermis overlying a densely fibrotic (sclerotic) dermis. It carries a small but real long-term risk of progression to vulvar squamous cell carcinoma, so biopsy-confirmed cases need ongoing follow-up. This thinning-plus-fibrosis pattern is the key histologic distinguishing feature from thickening vulvar dermatoses.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lichen simplex chronicus is characterized by epidermal thickening (hyperkeratosis and acanthosis) from chronic scratching, the opposite histologic pattern from the thinning seen in lichen sclerosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia shows dysplastic, disordered squamous epithelium with atypia, not the simple thinning-plus-dermal-fibrosis pattern described here.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Extramammary Paget disease shows large, pale malignant epithelial cells infiltrating the epidermis (Paget cells), a distinct histologic picture from lichen sclerosis's epidermal thinning and dermal fibrosis.

questions.learning_objective: Vulvar lichen sclerosis presents with thinning of the epidermis and dermal fibrosis

questions.title: A transurethral resection of the prostate specimen shows catheter-related fibrosis and a lymphocyte-predominant infiltrate, with a negative urine culture. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.question: A transurethral resection of the prostate specimen shows catheter-related fibrosis and a lymphocyte-predominant infiltrate, with a negative urine culture. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Correct. Chronic cystitis can arise from chronic irritation and instrumentation, such as long-standing catheter use or a transurethral resection specimen, rather than from an active bacterial infection; a negative urine culture together with catheter-related submucosal fibrosis and a predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate favors this chronic, non-infective process. This pattern is distinguished from acute bacterial cystitis, which is culture-positive with a predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate. Recognizing this culture-negative, lymphocyte-predominant pattern avoids unnecessary antibiotic treatment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Acute bacterial cystitis is defined by a positive urine culture and a predominantly neutrophilic (not lymphocytic) inflammatory infiltrate, the opposite of what is described here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Emphysematous cystitis is a gas-forming infection typically seen in diabetic patients, with gas visible within the bladder wall on imaging, not a culture-negative lymphocytic pattern.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Malacoplakia is characterized by von Hansemann histiocytes with Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, a distinct histologic picture from catheter-related fibrosis with a lymphocytic infiltrate.

questions.learning_objective: Culture-negative chronic cystitis after transurethral resection of the prostate is characterized by catheter-related fibrosis and lymphocyte-predominant inflammation

questions.title: A bladder biopsy shows keratinized epithelium invading the underlying stroma in sheets and nests, with many cells showing keratin pearls. What does this histologic pattern indicate?
questions.question: A bladder biopsy shows keratinized epithelium invading the underlying stroma in sheets and nests, with many cells showing keratin pearls. What does this histologic pattern indicate?

options.B: Invasive, poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma

explanations.A: Correct. Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder is graded by how closely the tumor recapitulates normal squamous epithelium; keratinized sheets and nests of malignant cells invading the stroma, with keratin pearls (concentric whorls of keratinization), are the classic hallmark of well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Keratin pearl formation reflects a high degree of squamous differentiation, not a more aggressive or poorly differentiated tumor. Recognizing this histologic marker of good differentiation is a key uropathology teaching point.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma lacks obvious keratinization and forms less organized sheets of atypical cells, the opposite of the prominent keratin pearl formation described here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Non-invasive (in situ) squamous carcinoma remains confined to the epithelium without breaching the basement membrane, whereas this specimen explicitly shows invasion of the underlying stroma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transitional (urothelial) cell carcinoma arises from and resembles normal urothelium, without the keratinized squamous morphology and keratin pearls described in this specimen.

questions.learning_objective: Invasive, well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder is characterized histologically by keratinized nests invading the stroma with keratin pearl formation

questions.title: An Egyptian man with a history of urinary schistosomiasis has a bladder mass; microscopy shows keratinizing changes of the epithelium. Which histologic type of bladder carcinoma is most likely?
questions.question: An Egyptian man with a history of urinary schistosomiasis has a bladder mass; microscopy shows keratinizing changes of the epithelium. Which histologic type of bladder carcinoma is most likely?

explanations.A: Correct. Chronic infection with Schistosoma haematobium, endemic in Egypt, causes persistent bladder wall inflammation from deposited ova, driving squamous metaplasia of the normally transitional bladder epithelium; this metaplastic epithelium is a well-recognized precursor to squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder. Microscopic keratinization of the epithelium in a patient with this history and geography is a classic exam pairing, distinct from the transitional cell carcinoma that dominates in non-endemic regions. This etiologic association is one of the best-known chronic-inflammation-to-metaplasia-to-carcinoma sequences in pathology teaching.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Transitional (urothelial) cell carcinoma is the dominant bladder cancer type in non-schistosomiasis-endemic regions, not the classic schistosomiasis-associated type, which is squamous.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenocarcinoma of the bladder is a distinct, less common subtype usually linked to urachal remnants or intestinal metaplasia, not the classic schistosomiasis association.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Small cell carcinoma of the bladder is a rare, highly aggressive neuroendocrine tumor type, not the classic schistosomiasis-associated histology.

questions.learning_objective: Chronic urinary schistosomiasis in Egypt is a classic cause of bladder squamous cell carcinoma, presenting with keratinized epithelial changes

questions.title: A 59-year-old man with flank pain and microscopic hematuria is found to have a 6 cm variegated renal mass; nephrectomy shows nests of cells with clear cytoplasm (clear cell renal cell carcinoma). Which of the following is LEAST likely to be an associated finding?
questions.question: A 59-year-old man with flank pain and microscopic hematuria is found to have a 6 cm variegated renal mass; nephrectomy shows nests of cells with clear cytoplasm (clear cell renal cell carcinoma). Which of the following is LEAST likely to be an associated finding?

explanations.A: Correct. Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is well known for a range of paraneoplastic manifestations, including fever, polycythemia, hypercalcemia, and a reversible hepatic dysfunction syndrome (Stauffer syndrome) that resolves after tumor resection. True hepatitis, meaning genuine hepatic inflammation from an infectious or toxic cause, is not among these classic RCC-associated findings, which is why it is the correct answer to a "least likely" question among these options. Distinguishing Stauffer syndrome's abnormal liver function tests from true hepatitis is the key discriminating point here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Polycythemia, from ectopic erythropoietin secretion by the tumor, is a well-recognized paraneoplastic finding in renal cell carcinoma, making it a likely (not least likely) association.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hypercalcemia, from tumor secretion of parathyroid hormone-related peptide, is a well-recognized paraneoplastic finding in renal cell carcinoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Fever is a classic constitutional paraneoplastic finding in renal cell carcinoma, part of its recognized presentation alongside flank pain, hematuria, and a palpable mass.

questions.subject: renal
questions.learning_objective: Renal cell carcinoma with clear cell histology does not characteristically present with hepatitis as an associated (paraneoplastic) finding

questions.title: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for end-stage renal disease (ESRD)?
questions.question: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for end-stage renal disease (ESRD)?

options.D: A family history of polycystic kidney disease

explanations.A: Correct. Obesity is a recognized modifiable risk factor for chronic kidney disease progressing to end-stage renal disease, acting both indirectly, by promoting hypertension and type 2 diabetes, and directly, through obesity-related glomerulopathy from glomerular hyperfiltration injury. Because it is modifiable through weight management, it is an important target for ESRD prevention efforts. This distinguishes it from non-modifiable risk factors such as age, sex, or inherited disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Age is a non-modifiable risk factor; while advancing age raises ESRD risk, it cannot itself be changed by intervention.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Male sex is a non-modifiable demographic risk factor associated with several causes of ESRD, but it cannot be modified.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A family history of polycystic kidney disease reflects a fixed genetic risk that cannot be modified, unlike obesity.

questions.title: Which of the following groups is least susceptible to urinary tract infection?
questions.question: Which of the following groups is least susceptible to urinary tract infection?

explanations.A: Correct. Among adults, men have the lowest baseline susceptibility to urinary tract infection, mainly because the male urethra is considerably longer than the female urethra and lies farther from the perianal/vaginal flora that seed most ascending UTIs, and normal prostatic secretions have some antibacterial activity. Male UTI risk does rise later in life with benign prostatic hyperplasia and instrumentation, but this does not change the general baseline comparison. Women, by contrast, are far more susceptible throughout most of adult life because of their short urethra.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Adult women, because of their short urethra and its proximity to periurethral flora, are substantially more susceptible to UTI than adult men, not less.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pregnancy further increases UTI susceptibility, through urinary stasis from progesterone-mediated ureteral relaxation and mechanical compression by the gravid uterus, making pregnant women more, not less, susceptible.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sexual activity increases UTI risk by introducing periurethral bacteria into the bladder (the mechanism behind "honeymoon cystitis"), making sexually active young women more, not less, susceptible.

questions.learning_objective: Adult males are the group least susceptible to urinary tract infection among the general adult population

questions.title: All of the following statements regarding end-stage renal disease (ESRD) are true EXCEPT?
questions.question: All of the following statements regarding end-stage renal disease (ESRD) are true EXCEPT?

options.A: Analgesic nephropathy is more common in men than in women
options.B: Diabetes mellitus is a leading cause of ESRD
options.C: Hypertension is a leading cause of ESRD

explanations.A: Correct (the false statement, and so the correct answer to this EXCEPT question). Analgesic nephropathy, chronic renal damage from long-term heavy analgesic use, is actually more common in women than in men, which stands in contrast to most other major causes of end-stage renal disease that are more common in men; this reflects a higher prevalence of chronic analgesic overuse among women in the populations where this association has been most studied. Because the statement claims the opposite (more common in men), it is the false statement being asked for.
explanations.B: Incorrect as an answer (it is a TRUE statement). Diabetes mellitus is one of the leading causes of end-stage renal disease worldwide, through diabetic nephropathy.
explanations.C: Incorrect as an answer (it is a TRUE statement). Hypertension is one of the leading causes of end-stage renal disease, through hypertensive nephrosclerosis.
explanations.D: Incorrect as an answer (it is a TRUE statement). Chronic glomerulonephritis is a well-recognized pathway to progressive kidney damage and end-stage renal disease.

questions.learning_objective: Analgesic nephropathy is more common in women than in men, contrary to the pattern for most other causes of end-stage renal disease

questions.title: Which of the following is a primary method of prevention of renal disease?
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary method of prevention of renal disease?

options.B: Screening asymptomatic adults for urine albumin

explanations.A: Correct. Primary prevention aims to stop disease before it starts by controlling underlying risk factors, and because hypertension is one of the leading causes of chronic kidney disease and its progression to end-stage renal disease, effective blood pressure control is a core primary prevention strategy for renal disease. This is distinguished from strategies aimed at people who already have early or established disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Screening asymptomatic individuals for urine albumin to catch early, otherwise silent kidney disease is secondary prevention (early detection), not primary prevention.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dialysis manages patients who already have established renal failure, which is tertiary prevention (limiting the impact of established disease), not primary prevention.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Renal transplantation, like dialysis, is a tertiary-prevention-level intervention for patients with established end-stage renal disease, not a primary prevention measure.

questions.learning_objective: Control of hypertension is a primary method of preventing renal disease
